title: The 8 Levels of Zillow Scrolling
house: A bustling neon-lit fruit and vegetable metropolis called Orchard City, where skyscrapers are shaped like giant stacked crates and digital currency numbers glow fiercely on every forehead.
catchphrase: The number never lies, but the square footage always does.
links: Level 1 mentions the grumpy pineapple barista at Metro Cafe who drops gold coins into a tip jar.
Level 2's ruined kitchen features the exact same leaky faucet that floods the apartment in Level 5.
Level 3's real estate agent drops off a brochure that ends up on the floor in Level 7.
Level 4's burnt toast scent drifts through the open window into Level 6's hallway.
Level 5's stolen package is the exact mystery delivery tracked down in Level 8.

levels.name: Pip, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 1. Level 1: 0 dollars in savings, yet I have 84 open tabs of luxury mansions in Bel-Air. I am Pip, a stressed green apple with a bruised cheek, sitting on the sticky floor of a cramped subway car at 2 AM. My phone screen glows blindingly bright, displaying a seven-million-dollar beachfront villa with an infinity pool. Look at this loser, pretending she is buying a mansion with zero dollars on her forehead. Tears prick my eyes as I clutch my cracked smartphone tighter. You will never even afford the driveway, little fruit. My chest tightens with absolute shame, and I furiously swipe to close all the tabs. What hidden text message did the landlord send right after kicking her out? You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Brix, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 2. Level 2: 1,850 dollars a month salary, and I spent three hours touring a 12 million dollar penthouse in downtown Manhattan. I am Brix, a zesty yellow lemon person with a permanent sour frown, wiping down the stainless steel espresso machine at Metro Cafe. Stop wasting your life on housing apps, tiny citrus, nobody wants a broker with your wage. My teeth grind together so hard my jaw aches. I am just looking for a better future, I snap back, my voice trembling. Nobody wants a broker with your wage. He laughs coldly, flashing his glowing Level 4 badge of 6,200 dollars. My face burns hot red with absolute humiliation as I pick up the crumpled paper. Whose name was actually signed on the mysterious cashier's check? You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Brooke, 29, Graphic Designer
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 3. Level 3: 3,400 dollars net income, yet I spent my entire weekend attending open houses for multi-million dollar estates I will never own. I am Brooke, a vibrant head of curly green broccoli florets, standing in the marble foyer of a modern mansion. You brought a freelance designer to a five-million-dollar showing? How utterly embarrassing for you. My cheeks burn instantly and I grip the strap of my canvas tote bag until my knuckles turn white. I am seriously interested, I stammer, my voice echoing off the vaulted ceilings. How utterly embarrassing for you. She laughs in my face, her glowing Level 5 badge flashing 9,800 dollars on her pink-scaled forehead. What secret blueprint was folded inside the real estate agent's leather briefcase? You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Tangelo, 31, Mid-Level Manager
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 4. Level 4: 6,200 dollars a month, and I am still priced out of every decent neighborhood in the city. I am Tangelo, a smooth orange-peel man wearing my favorite cashmere turtleneck, standing inside a sleek glass-walled condo. You are taking up space reserved for actual buyers, step aside peasant. My breath catches in my throat and my orange skin flushes a deep, angry crimson. I earn a very respectable salary, I snap back, stepping forward. Step aside peasant. She gives a harsh, patronizing chuckle, revealing her glowing Level 7 badge of 22,000 dollars on her crown. Why did the security guard immediately lock the front gates after she stepped outside? You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Pitaya, 34, Senior Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 5. Level 5: 9,800 dollars a month, yet I just lost my dream house to an all-cash offer for the third time this month. I am Pitaya, a vibrant pink dragonfruit woman with spiky green crown leaves, sitting alone in my rented studio apartment surrounded by architectural blueprints. Still crying over houses you can't actually win, dragon? My temper flares instantly and my spikes bristle with pure rage. Watch your mouth, barkeep, you do not know my struggles, I snap, slamming my laptop shut. At least I don't pretend to be a tycoon. He flashes his pathetic Level 2 badge of 1,850 dollars and scoffs. Who transferred 50,000 dollars into her account right before the auction closed? You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Congo, 39, Tech Executive
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 6. Level 6: 14,500 dollars monthly net, and I still spend my weekends bidding on multi-million dollar compounds just to feel powerful. I am Congo, a sturdy brown coconut man with a hard fibrous husk, wearing a custom charcoal suit. As I step out of my luxury sports car, a battered green apple intern named Pip approaches me asking for spare change. Get a real job instead of staring at luxury listings on a broken phone, loser. I sneer, flashing my glowing Level 6 badge of 14,500 dollars to remind everyone who rules this city. I have wealth, power, and absolute control over every property deal in Orchard City. As I walk up the courthouse steps to finalize my latest mansion purchase, the bailiff hands me an unexpected legal document. What dark secret was written inside the property deed handed to her by the judge? You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Melon, 55, The Grand Mayor
levels.story: The 8 levels of endless property portal scrolling. Level 8. The final level. Level 8: Unlimited numbers on my forehead, yet I own every single square foot of Orchard City, and I started just like all of you. I am Melon, a massive striped watermelon elder with a polished smooth rind, sitting in the towering glass penthouse overlooking the entire metropolis. Every single character you saw in Levels 1 through 7 worked inside my properties, drank my coffee, and scrolled through my portal apps. You built an empire on broken dreams and fake listings. I smile calmly, tapping my glowing forehead where the infinity symbol burns in bright neon light. The number on your forehead never defined your worth, it only measured your hunger. Which topic of our digital life obsession should we uncover in the next series?
